beats.narration_text: Bonjour — this is Liam, in for Komal. People picture luxury plus A.I. as a chatbot on the counter. Wrong picture. Watch what L V M H actually built — and why Tiffany's advisor is the tell.

beats.narration_text: Loud A.I. puts a bot between the house and the client. Quiet tech does the opposite. L V M H's own line: technology everywhere, visible nowhere. The machine briefs the advisor. The human still owns the room.
beats.tts_normalized_text: Loud, A.I. puts a bot between the house and the client. Quiet tech does the opposite. L V M H's own line: technology everywhere, visible nowhere. The machine briefs the advisor. The human still owns the room.

beats.narration_text: Seventy-five maisons. Louis Vuitton, Dior, Tiffany, Celine. They built a Google Cloud data platform so each house keeps its own client data — then layers agents on top. C I O Franck Le Moal: seamless, invisible, more dedicated attention without being intrusive. That is the design, not a slogan.

The brand example is Tiffany. Each advisor has a client list. Now they have an A.I. chat on that list — tastes, affinities, a piece the client might not have known about. The client never talks to the model. The advisor does. Then they look up and do the job luxury actually sells: time, and a relationship.

show.event: The client never meets the model.

beats.narration_text: Quiet does not mean small. June twenty twenty-five: more than forty thousand staff users a month, more than one point five million queries. Finance, retail, legal, H R — internal agents. This is back-of-house intelligence at group scale, not a storefront stunt.

What changes next — three bets they already named. One: a continuous client story, not scattered touchpoints. Two: the unique jewel routed to the right salon — Zurich, not everywhere. Three: if A.I. does not raise desire for the house, it does not count as success.

layers.title: The unique piece, the right salon
Desire as the KPI
layers.sub: If it doesn’t raise want, it doesn’t scale

beats.narration_text: Louis Vuitton's line at N R F: A.I. never replaces creativity — it amplifies it. Materials, colours, briefing. The atelier and the relationship stay human. Houses that chase a gimmicky bot will fail to scale. Houses that arm the advisor will look unchanged — until you notice the conversation got sharper.

Houses that chase a gimmicky bot will fail to scale. Houses that arm the advisor will look unchanged, until you notice the conversation got sharper.

beats.narration_text: Let's recap with Claude. Luxury A.I. is quiet tech: it arms the advisor, it does not replace the salon. Tiffany is the receipt. Scale is already staff-wide. The next chapter is a continuous story, scarcity routed with care, and desire as the only KPI that matters. Design judgment: if the client can see the model, the house already lost.

artifactLines: Mechanism: LVMH quiet tech — everywhere, visible nowhere. Google Cloud platform; maisons keep their own client data.
Receipt: Tiffany client advisors chat with an AI on taste and affinity; the client still meets a human.
Scale (June 2025): 40,000+ monthly staff users, 1.5M+ queries — internal, not a boutique bot.
Next: continuous client story · unique piece to the right salon · desire as the KPI.
The rule: if the client can see the model, the house already lost.

See whether the house is arming the salon — or decorating the homepage.
